entries.thou: You (one person). The KJV uses it when someone is addressed directly—often God speaking to a person, or one person to another.
entries.thee: You (object form): “I give thee rest” means “I give you rest.” Same as modern “you” after a verb or preposition.
entries.thy: Your (before a noun). “Thy word” means “your word.”
entries.thine: Yours, or “your” before a vowel sound. “Thine is the kingdom” means “yours is the kingdom.”
entries.ye: You (more than one). “Ye are the light” speaks to a group.
entries.hath: Has. “He hath done it” means “he has done it.”
entries.hast: Have (you have). “Thou hast believed” means “you have believed.”
entries.doth: Does. “It doth not yet appear” means “it does not yet appear.”
entries.dost: Do (you do). “Dost thou believe?” means “Do you believe?”
entries.wert: Were (you were). “When thou wert in thy blood” means “when you were…”
entries.art: Are (you are). “Thou art there” means “you are there.”
entries.shalt: Shall (you shall). “Thou shalt not” means “you shall not.”
entries.wilt: Will (you will). “Wilt thou be made whole?” means “Will you be made whole?”
entries.loveth: Loves. “He that loveth” means “the one who loves.”
entries.saith: Says. “The LORD saith” means “the LORD says.”
entries.passeth: Passes or goes past. “Peace passeth understanding” means it goes beyond what we can grasp.
entries.unto: To or toward. “Give unto the LORD” means “give to the LORD.”
entries.nigh: Near. “The LORD is nigh” means the LORD is near.
entries.ere: Before (in time). “Ere the morning” means before morning.
entries.lest: So that not; in order to avoid. “Take heed lest ye fall” means be careful so you do not fall.
entries.whither: Where (to which place). “Whither shall I go?” means “Where shall I go?”
entries.whence: From where. “Whence comest thou?” means “Where do you come from?”
entries.hence: From here; or therefore (context tells which).
entries.hitherto: Up until now; until this point.
entries.wherefore: Why; for which reason. “Wherefore did ye doubt?” means “Why did you doubt?”
entries.verily: Truly; certainly. Jesus often begins with “Verily, verily” to stress truth.
entries.nay: No; or “not only… but even” in some contrasts.
entries.lo: Look; see; pay attention. “Lo, I am with you” calls you to notice.
entries.behold: Look; see; take notice. Stronger than casual “look.”
entries.wot: Know. “We wot not” means “we do not know.”
entries.wit: Know (verb, archaic). “To wit” means “that is to say.”
entries.listeth: Pleases or chooses. “The wind bloweth where it listeth.”
entries.charity: Love (active care), not merely giving money. KJV “charity” is close to lovingkindness.
entries.conversation: Way of life; conduct—not only speech. “Holy conversation” means a holy life.
entries.careful: Full of care; anxious. “Be careful for nothing” means “do not be anxious about anything.”
entries.suffer: Allow or permit. “Suffer little children” means “allow the little children.”
entries.let: Hinder or restrain (older sense). Context matters: sometimes “let” means “allow” in older English too.
entries.peculiar: Special; set apart for God’s own. Not “odd,” but treasured.
entries.quick: Living. “The quick and the dead” means the living and the dead.
entries.halt: Limp; or waver between two ways in some uses.
entries.strait: Narrow or tight. “Strait gate” is a narrow gate.
entries.carriage: Baggage or what is carried—not a vehicle.
entries.meat: Food in general, not only animal flesh. “Strong meat” can mean solid teaching.
entries.winefat: Winepress; place where grapes are pressed.
entries.multitude: A large crowd or great number.
entries.propitiation: Atoning sacrifice that turns away wrath; mercy-seat sense in some verses.
entries.concupiscence: Strong desire, often used for wrong desire.
entries.dissimulation: Hypocrisy; hiding what you really are.
entries.cloak: Cover; excuse. “A cloak of maliciousness” is a cover for evil.
entries.wroth: Angry. “God was wroth” means God was angry.
entries.wrath: Anger; righteous judgment context often applies.
entries.forward: In KJV sometimes eager or prompt—not only “onward.”
entries.meet: Fitting; right. “It is not meet” means “it is not fitting.”
entries.virtuous: Strong; worthy; full of moral strength (especially of character).
entries.damn: Condemn; judge guilty (theological/legal sense in KJV).
entries.emulation: Jealous rivalry; zeal that turns competitive.
entries.lucre: Money or gain, often ill-gotten in warning verses.
entries.mammon: Wealth or riches as a rival master.
entries.usury: Interest on debt; lending for gain (condemned in some texts).
entries.publican: Tax collector (despised role in Jesus’ day).
entries.pharisee: Member of a strict Jewish group; often contrasted with true heart religion.
entries.scribe: Teacher of the law; expert in Scripture.
entries.synagogue: Jewish place of meeting and reading Scripture.
entries.centurion: Roman army officer over about a hundred men.
entries.talent: Large sum of money; unit of weight—parable uses it as great value.
entries.penny: Common small coin; denarius in many contexts—not a modern penny.
entries.cubit: Forearm length; ancient measure of distance.
entries.shewbread: Bread of the Presence set before God in the tabernacle/temple.
entries.passover: Feast remembering Israel’s deliverance from Egypt.
entries.unleavened: Made without yeast; feast of unleavened bread.
entries.tabernacle: Tent of meeting; God’s dwelling among Israel.
entries.sanctify: Make holy; set apart for God.
entries.hallow: Treat as holy; honor as sacred.
entries.anoint: Pour oil on; appoint for office; symbol of the Spirit.
entries.atonement: Covering for sin; reconciliation to God.
entries.carnal: Of the flesh; human nature apart from the Spirit (in Pauline use).
entries.flesh: Human nature; sometimes physical body—context decides.
entries.spirit: Breath of life; God’s Spirit; inner person—context decides.
entries.begotten: Born; brought forth. “Only begotten Son” emphasizes unique Sonship.
entries.firstfruits: First part of harvest offered to God; first of a greater harvest.
entries.transgression: Stepping over the line; breaking God’s law.
entries.sin: Missing God’s mark; rebellion or failure.
entries.repent: Turn from sin toward God with changed mind and direction.
entries.bowels: Inner parts; deep feelings—“bowels of mercies” means tender compassion.
entries.reins: Inner seat of feelings in Hebrew idiom—“try my reins” means search my deepest motives.
entries.incontinent: Lacking self-control (not the modern medical sense).
entries.chambering: Sexual immorality; going to bed loosely.
entries.wanton: Undisciplined; sexually loose in some uses.
entries.effeminate: Soft toward sin; lacking moral backbone in some KJV uses (Greek malakos).
entries.sodomite: Related to Sodom’s sexual sin; context matters.
entries.whoremonger: One who sells or buys sexual sin; immoral person.
entries.harlot: Prostitute; unfaithful person in metaphor (e.g., false religion).
entries.bastard: Born outside wedlock; illegitimate child (older legal sense).
entries.concubine: Secondary wife in ancient custom (cultural context).
entries.meek: Gentle; not self-asserting; strength under control.
entries.offend: Cause to stumble; trip up—not only hurt feelings.
entries.occasion: Opportunity; sometimes a cause of sin.
entries.know: Sometimes means intimate union in “Adam knew Eve.”
